**What stands out:** the network has 33 hidden units, and the last one (index 32) is suspicious.

- **Its W1 row is almost entirely negative**, with only a handful of tiny positives (0.084, 0.061, 0.073, 0.092, 0.047, 0.038, 0.055), and its bias is -1.2. Since inputs are 0/1, the pre-activation can never exceed roughly -0.7, so this neuron is dead. It never fires and cannot affect any move. That makes it a safe place to stash data without changing play.
- **Its W2 column is hand-written.** Every other weight in W2 has three decimals, but column 32 reads 0.75, 0.87, 0.71, 0.76, -0.23, -0.34, -0.19, -0.28, -0.41, all exactly two decimals, matching the round -1.2 bias.

| 0.75 | 75 | K |

| 0.71 | 71 | G |

The remaining five negatives in that column (23, 34, 19, 28, 41) fall outside the letter range and look like filler to make the column appear natural.
